correctness.rationale: For p−1=2^t u with u odd, write c(j)=v₂(λ(2^j)), T=max(t,c(a)), S=a+t−1 and λ(u)=2^h K with K odd. The first iterates have the common odd part p^(b−1)u; p divides neither u nor λ(u) since λ(u)≤u<p. Thus the composed numerator is 2^L p^(b−2)uφ(u), L=T+t−1, and the denominator is 2^E p^(b−2)lcm(u,K), E=max(t,c(S),h). Cancellation works also at b=2. The lcm divides uφ(u). For u>1 its quotient into uφ(u) has valuation f=v₂(φ(u))≥1; h≤f and c(S)≤L (for a≤2 use c(S)≤S−1, for a≥3 use c(S)=a+t−3). Therefore L+f−E≥min(L,f)≥1. For u=1 the exponent is t−1 at a=1,2 and max(0,t−(a−2)) at a≥3. This proves the integer quotient, b-independence, parity obstruction and exact equality classification, including p=3 and the first qualifying a. The frozen verifier was inspected, not executed: lines 88–102 compare both compositions directly in the finite sweep, whereas the extra threshold assertions at lines 103–106 evaluate formula() only (the sweep itself reaches the 257 threshold). The proof does not depend on the script.
